subject.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels

question: Should CLI reseed history expose the persisted group sender fields as a nested `User (<sender>)` model-visible label, rather than retaining anonymous `User:` history for those turns?
rationale: The persistence contract is already merged, but displaying participant identity in model-visible historical prompts is an intentional session-context and trust-boundary choice that should be accepted by the relevant owner before merge.

options.title: Accept the nested sender label
options.body: Approve the existing three-field `__openclaw` contract for CLI historical rendering once the refreshed merge-head checks pass.

options.title: Keep anonymous CLI history
options.body: Decline model-visible sender attribution and close this renderer-only path while retaining the durable metadata for other owner-approved consumers.

recommendation.title: Accept the nested sender label
recommendation.body: Approve the existing three-field `__openclaw` contract for CLI historical rendering once the refreshed merge-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged durable sender-metadata contract that defines the data this PR would expose in CLI history.
